q: मध्य प्रदेश का कौन-सा पुरातात्विक स्थल अपने प्रागैतिहासिक पुरापाषाण एवं मध्यपाषाणकालीन शैलचित्रों (गुफा चित्रों) के लिए विश्वप्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Bhimbetka rock shelters (Raisen district, MP — discovered by V. S. Wakankar in 1957–58; UNESCO World Heritage Site) preserve prehistoric rock art from the Palaeolithic to historic periods.
• Exam Booster: Burzahom (Kashmir) = Neolithic pit-dwellings & dog burial with master; Mehrgarh (Balochistan) = earliest evidence of agriculture (wheat/barley); Koldihwa (UP, Belan Valley) = earliest rice evidence.
qe: Which archaeological site in Madhya Pradesh is world-famous for its prehistoric Palaeolithic and Mesolithic rock shelter paintings?

q: गुजरात का कौन-सा हड़प्पा स्थल अपने प्राचीन ईंटों से बने ज्वारीय 'गोदीवाड़ा' (Dockyard) के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Lothal (on the Bhogava River, Gujarat — excavated by S. R. Rao) featured a massive tidal dockyard, bead-making factory, and evidence of rice husk and double burial.
• Exam Booster: Dholavira (Gujarat, UNESCO 2021) = 3-tier town planning & sophisticated water management; Kalibangan (Rajasthan) = ploughed field & fire altars; Surkotada = horse bones.
qe: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is famous for its ancient brick-lined tidal 'Dockyard' (गोदीवाड़ा)?

q:
निम्नलिखित सिंधु घाटी स्थलों को उनके तटवर्ती नदियों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. हड़प्पा — (a) सिंधु
2. मोहनजोदड़ो — (b) रावी
3. कालीबंगा — (c) हिंडन
4. आलमगीरपुर — (d) घग्गर
e:
Correct matching: Harappa — Ravi (1-b, excavated by Daya Ram Sahni, 1921); Mohenjo-daro — Indus (2-a, R. D. Banerji, 1922); Kalibangan — Ghaggar (3-d); Alamgirpur (Meerut, UP — easternmost Harappan site) — Hindon (4-c).
• Exam Booster: Four extreme boundaries of IVC: North = Manda (J&K, Chenab); South = Daimabad (Maharashtra, Pravara); East = Alamgirpur (UP, Hindon); West = Sutkagendor (Balochistan, Dasht).
qe:
Match the following Indus Valley sites with the rivers on whose banks they were situated:
1. Harappa — (a) Indus (Sindhu)
2. Mohenjo-daro — (b) Ravi
3. Kalibangan — (c) Hindon
4. Alamgirpur — (d) Ghaggar

q: हड़प्पा सभ्यता के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: वृहत् स्नानागार और कांस्य की 'नर्तकी' मोहनजोदड़ो से प्राप्त हुए हैं
हड़प्पा की मुहरें मुख्यतः सेलखड़ी (स्टीटाइट) की बनी थीं
हड़प्पा के लोगों को लोहे की धातुकर्म का विस्तृत ज्ञान था और वे लोहे के हल का उपयोग करते थे
हड़प्पा की लिपि भावचित्रात्मक है और बूस्ट्रोफेडन शैली में लिखी गई है
e:
Statement C is NOT correct: The Indus Valley Civilization was a BRONZE AGE (कांस्ययुगीन) civilization; iron was unknown to the Harappans (iron came into widespread use in India during the Later Vedic / Painted Grey Ware period around 1000 BCE).
• Exam Booster: Boustrophedon script runs right-to-left on the first line and left-to-right on the next.
qe: Which of the following statements regarding the Harappan Civilization is NOT correct?
oe: The Great Bath and the bronze 'Dancing Girl' were excavated at Mohenjo-daro
Harappan seals were predominantly made of steatite (soapstone)
Harappan people had extensive knowledge of iron metallurgy and used iron ploughshares
The Harappan script is pictographic and written in boustrophedon style

q: उत्तर प्रदेश के प्रतापगढ़ जिले के किस स्थल से गंगा घाटी में मध्यपाषाणकालीन मानव कंकालों और हड्डी के आभूषणों के प्राचीनतम साक्ष्य मिले हैं?
e:
Sarai Nahar Rai, Mahadaha, and Damdama in Pratapgarh district (UP) are landmark Mesolithic sites yielding human burials, hearths, and bone/antler ornaments.
• Exam Booster: Atranjikhera (Etah, UP) is famous for earliest Painted Grey Ware (PGW) and iron artefacts in the Ganga valley.
qe: Which site in Uttar Pradesh's Pratapgarh district has yielded the earliest Mesolithic evidence of human skeletons and bone ornaments in the Ganga Valley?

q: ऋग्वेद के किस मंडल में प्रसिद्ध 'गायत्री मंत्र' (सविता को समर्पित) और किस मंडल में 'पुरुष सूक्त' (चार वर्णों का उल्लेख) मिलता है?
e:
Gayatri Mantra (composed by Vishwamitra) is in the 3rd Mandala of Rigveda, and Purusha Sukta is in the 10th Mandala.
• Exam Booster: 7th Mandala describes the Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna War on the Parushni/Ravi river); 9th Mandala is entirely dedicated to Soma.
qe: Which Mandala of the Rigveda contains the famous 'Gayatri Mantra' (dedicated to Savitri) and which Mandala contains the 'Purusha Sukta' (mentioning the four Varnas)?

q: ऋग्वैदिक काल में दो लोकप्रिय जन-सभाएँ कौन-सी थीं—एक संपूर्ण जन की आम सभा और दूसरी श्रेष्ठ/वरिष्ठ जनों की छोटी परिषद?
e:
'Samiti' was the general folk assembly (which elected the Rajan) and 'Sabha' was a smaller council of elders; Atharvaveda calls Sabha and Samiti the "two daughters of Prajapati".
• Exam Booster: 'Vidatha' was the oldest Vedic assembly (religious/distributive), in which women actively participated.
qe: In the Rigvedic period, what were the two popular tribal assemblies called—one a general assembly of the whole folk and the other a smaller council of elders?

q: गौतम बुद्ध ने अपना प्रथम उपदेश ('धर्मचक्रप्रवर्तन') कहाँ दिया था?
e:
Buddha delivered his first sermon to five ascetics at Deer Park (Mrigadava / Rishipatana) in Sarnath near Varanasi.
• Exam Booster: Four key Buddhist sites: Lumbini (Birth), Bodh Gaya (Enlightenment / Nirvana), Sarnath (First Sermon / Dharmachakrapravartana), Kushinagar (Mahaparinirvana).
qe: Where did Gautama Buddha deliver his first sermon ('Dharmachakrapravartana')?

q: जैन धर्म के 23वें तीर्थंकर (वाराणसी में जन्मे, जिनका प्रतीक चिह्न सर्प है) कौन थे, और उनके चार महाव्रतों में पाँचवाँ महाव्रत 'ब्रह्मचर्य' किसने जोड़ा?
e:
Parshvanatha (23rd Tirthankara, son of King Ashvasena of Kashi) taught 4 vows (Satya, Ahimsa, Asteya, Aparigraha), to which the 24th Tirthankara Vardhamana Mahavira added the 5th vow—Brahmacharya.
• Exam Booster: Rishabhanatha (Adinatha, symbol Bull) was the 1st Tirthankara; Mahavira's symbol is Lion. Jain councils: 1st at Pataliputra (Sthulabhadra), 2nd at Vallabhi (Devardhi Kshamasramana).
qe: Who was the 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism (born in Varanasi, whose symbol is the Serpent) and who added the fifth vow 'Brahmacharya' to his four vows?

q: छठी शताब्दी ई.पू. के निम्नलिखित 16 महाजनपदों और उनकी राजधानियों का कौन-सा युग्म सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e:
Statement D is NOT correctly matched: Panchala's capitals were Ahichhatra (North Panchala, Bareilly) and Kampilya (South Panchala, Farrukhabad), whereas Varanasi was the capital of 'Kashi'.
• Exam Booster: 8 of the 16 Mahajanapadas were located in present-day Uttar Pradesh (Kashi, Kosala, Malla, Vatsa, Chedi, Kuru, Panchala, Surasena).
qe: Which of the following 16 Mahajanapadas (6th century BCE) and their capitals is NOT correctly matched?

q: सेल्यूकस निकेटर द्वारा चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में भेजा गया यूनानी राजदूत कौन था, जिसने 'इंडिका' की रचना की?
e:
Megasthenes resided at Pataliputra in Chandragupta Maurya's court and wrote 'Indica' (describing municipal administration by 6 committees of 5 members each and 7 social classes).
• Exam Booster: Deimachus visited Bindusara's court; Fa-Hien visited Chandragupta II's court; Hiuen Tsang visited Harshavardhana's court.
qe: Who was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, who authored 'Indica'?

q: मौर्य प्रशासन में सम्राट अशोक द्वारा अपने राज्याभिषेक के 14वें वर्ष (पाँचवें वृहद शिलालेख में उल्लिखित) में धम्म प्रचार एवं लोक-कल्याण हेतु नियुक्त उच्चाधिकारी क्या कहलाते थे?
e:
Ashoka created the post of 'Dhamma Mahamattas' (धम्म महामात्र) to promote moral conduct, religious tolerance, and welfare of prisoners/poor.
• Exam Booster: In Kautilya's Arthashastra, 'Samaharta' was Chief Revenue Collector and 'Sannidhata' was Chief Treasurer; 'Sitadhyaksha' supervised crown lands (Sita).
qe: In Mauryan administration, what were the high-ranking officers appointed by Emperor Ashoka in his 14th regnal year (mentioned in Major Rock Edict V) to spread Dhamma and oversee welfare called?

q: अशोक के किस अभिलेख में उनका व्यक्तिगत नाम 'अशोक' स्पष्ट रूप से उत्कीर्ण मिलता है (गुर्जरा, नेट्टूर और उडेगोलम के साथ)?
e:
In most edicts Ashoka is titled 'Devanampiya Piyadasi', while his personal name 'Ashoka' appears in only four minor rock edicts: Maski (Karnataka), Gujarra (MP), Nettur, and Udegolam.
• Exam Booster: Rummindei (Lumbini) Pillar Edict records Ashoka's visit to Buddha's birthplace and reduction of land revenue (Bali) to 1/8th; Bhabru Edict records his faith in Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha.
qe: Which Ashokan inscription explicitly mentions his personal name 'Ashoka' (along with Gujarra, Nettur, and Udegolam)?

q: 185 ई.पू. में अंतिम मौर्य शासक बृहद्रथ की हत्या कर शुंग वंश की स्थापना किसने की थी?
e:
Mauryan commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga killed Brihadratha in 185 BCE and founded the Shunga dynasty; grammarian Patanjali ('Mahabhashya') was his contemporary and priest at his two Ashvamedha sacrifices.
• Exam Booster: Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty; Vasudeva founded the Kanva dynasty.
qe: Who assassinated the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha in 185 BCE and founded the Shunga Dynasty?

q: किस गुप्त सम्राट ने 'विक्रमादित्य' की उपाधि धारण की, पश्चिम भारत के शकों को पराजित कर चाँदी के सिक्के चलाए, और जिनके काल में चीनी यात्री फाह्यान भारत आया?
e:
Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (380–415 CE) defeated Shaka ruler Rudrasimha III, issued silver Rupaka coins, maintained the Navaratnas (Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Amarasimha, Dhanvantari), and hosted Fa-Hien.
• Exam Booster: Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda University; Skandagupta repulsed the Huna invasion (Bhitari Pillar Inscription, Ghazipur UP).
qe: Which Gupta emperor assumed the title 'Vikramaditya', issued silver coins after defeating the Shakas of western India, and hosted the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien?

q: महरौली (दिल्ली) का जंग-रहित 'लौह स्तंभ' किस शासक 'चंद्र' का उल्लेख करता है, जिनकी पहचान सामान्यतः की जाती है:
e:
The Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription praises King 'Chandra' (identified with Chandragupta II Vikramaditya) for his victories in Vanga (Bengal) and across the Indus (Bahlika).
• Exam Booster: The first epigraphic evidence of Sati in India comes from the Eran Inscription (510 CE, MP) of Gupta ruler Bhanugupta.
qe: The 'Iron Pillar' at Mehrauli (Delhi), famous for its rust-free metallurgy, mentions a ruler named 'Chandra' generally identified with:

q: हर्षवर्धन ने अपनी राजधानी थानेश्वर से उत्तर प्रदेश के किस प्रसिद्ध नगर में स्थानांतरित की थी, और जिनके शासनकाल में चीनी यात्री ह्वेनसांग भारत आया?
e:
Harshavardhana (606–647 CE) made Kannauj (Kanyakubja) his imperial capital; he also authored three Sanskrit plays: 'Nagananda', 'Ratnavali', and 'Priyadarshika'.
• Exam Booster: Harsha was defeated on the banks of the Narmada by Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II (Aihole Inscription by Ravikirti).
qe: Harshavardhana shifted his capital from Thanesar to which famous city in Uttar Pradesh, and hosted the Chinese Buddhist traveller Hiuen Tsang?

q: भारतीय इतिहास में कौन-सा दक्षिण भारतीय राजवंश अपने अत्यंत विकसित 'ग्राम स्वशासन' (सभा, उर और वारियम समितियाँ — उत्तरमेरुर अभिलेख में वर्णित) के लिए सर्वाधिक प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
The Imperial Cholas (specifically Parantaka I's Uttaramerur Inscription) established an exemplary autonomous village administration using the 'Kudavolai' (lottery) system for committee elections.
• Exam Booster: Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur; Rajendra I conquered Srivijaya (SE Asia) and assumed the title 'Gangaikondachola'.
qe: Which South Indian dynasty is most celebrated in Indian history for its highly developed 'Village Self-Government' (Sabha, Ur, and Variyam committees — documented in the Uttaramerur Inscription)?

q:
निम्नलिखित प्राचीन भारतीय विद्वानों को उनके प्रमुख ग्रंथों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. आर्यभट्ट — (a) बृहत्संहिता
2. वराहमिहिर — (b) अष्टाध्यायी
3. चरक — (c) आर्यभटीय
4. पाणिनि — (d) चरक संहिता
e:
Correct matching: Aryabhata — Aryabhatiya (1-c, place-value zero, π ≈ 3.1416, axial rotation of Earth); Varahamihira — Brihat Samhita & Panchasiddhantika (2-a); Charaka — Charaka Samhita (3-d, Ayurveda); Panini — Ashtadhyayi (4-b, Sanskrit grammar).
• Exam Booster: Sushruta ('Sushruta Samhita') is revered as the Father of Plastic Surgery; Brahmagupta authored 'Brahmasphutasiddhanta'.
qe:
Match the following ancient Indian scholars with their landmark works:
1. Aryabhata — (a) Brihat Samhita
2. Varahamihira — (b) Ashtadhyayi
3. Charaka — (c) Aryabhatiya
4. Panini — (d) Charaka Samhita

q: 1206 ई. में दिल्ली में 'गुलाम वंश' (ममलूक वंश) की स्थापना किसने की थी, जिन्हें 'लाख बख्श' (लाखों का दान देने वाला) कहा जाता था?
e:
Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1206–1210, capital Lahore) founded the Delhi Sultanate, initiated construction of Qutb Minar (completed by Iltutmish), and died playing Chaugan (polo).
• Exam Booster: Iltutmish introduced silver 'Tanka' & copper 'Jital', organized 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani' (Corps of Forty), and institutionalized the 'Iqta' system.
qe: Who founded the 'Slave Dynasty' (Mamluk Dynasty) in Delhi in 1206 CE and was known as 'Lakh Baksh' (giver of lakhs)?

q: किस दिल्ली सुल्तान ने 'बाजार नियंत्रण प्रणाली' (दीवान-ए-रियासत व शहना-ए-मंडी), 'दाग' (घोड़ों को दागना) और 'चेहरा/हुलिया' प्रथा प्रारंभ की?
e:
Alauddin Khalji (1296–1316) maintained a large standing army paid in cash via strict price controls (Diwan-i-Riyasat), measured agricultural land (Biswa), and established Diwan-i-Mustakhraj (arrears).
• Exam Booster: His general Malik Kafur led the Deccan campaigns (Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra, Madurai).
qe: Which Delhi Sultan introduced the 'Market Control Policy' (Diwan-i-Riyasat and Shahna-i-Mandi), 'Dagh' (branding of horses), and 'Chehra' (descriptive roll of soldiers)?

q: दिल्ली के किस सुल्तान ने 1504 ई. में 'आगरा' नगर की स्थापना की और भूमि मापन के लिए 'गज-ए-सिकंदरी' का प्रचलन किया?
e:
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 CE, made it his capital in 1506, introduced Gaj-i-Sikandari, and composed Persian poetry under the pen name 'Gulrukhi'.
• Exam Booster: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Jaunpur (in memory of Jauna Khan/Muhammad bin Tughlaq), Firozabad, Hisar, and Fatehabad.
qe: Which Sultan of Delhi founded the city of 'Agra' in 1504 CE and introduced the 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' (30-inch unit for land measurement)?

q:
दिल्ली सल्तनत के निम्नलिखित प्रशासनिक विभागों को उनके कार्यों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. दीवान-ए-अर्ज — (a) कृषि विभाग (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक)
2. दीवान-ए-अमीर कोही — (b) सैन्य विभाग (बलबन)
3. दीवान-ए-बंदगान — (c) दास विभाग (फिरोज शाह तुगलक)
4. दीवान-ए-खैरात — (d) दान विभाग (फिरोज शाह तुगलक)
e:
Correct matching: Diwan-i-Arz — Military (1-b, Balban); Diwan-i-Amir Kohi — Agriculture (2-a, MBT); Diwan-i-Bandagan — Slaves (3-c, FST); Diwan-i-Khairat — Charity (4-d, FST).
• Exam Booster: Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta ('Rihla') visited India during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign (1333 CE) and was appointed Qazi of Delhi.
qe:
Match the following administrative departments of the Delhi Sultanate with their functions:
1. Diwan-i-Arz — (a) Agriculture Department (Muhammad bin Tughlaq)
2. Diwan-i-Amir Kohi — (b) Military Department (Balban)
3. Diwan-i-Bandagan — (c) Slaves Department (Firoz Shah Tughlaq)
4. Diwan-i-Khairat — (d) Charity Department (Firoz Shah Tughlaq)

q: विजयनगर के तुलुव वंश के किस महान शासक ने तेलुगु राजनीति-ग्रंथ 'आमुक्तमाल्यद' की रचना की और 'अष्टदिग्गज' (तेनाली रामकृष्ण सहित) को संरक्षण दिया?
e:
Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE) was the greatest Vijayanagara emperor (called 'Andhra Bhoja'); Portuguese travellers Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa visited his court.
• Exam Booster: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 by Harihara & Bukka (Sangama dynasty); the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi, 1565) marked its decline.
qe: Which great ruler of the Tuluva Dynasty of Vijayanagara authored the Telugu political treatise 'Amuktamalyada' and patronized the 'Ashtadiggajas' (including Tenali Ramakrishna)?

q: पानीपत का प्रथम युद्ध किस वर्ष हुआ था, जिसमें बाबर ने तोपखाने और तुलुगमा युद्धनीति के प्रयोग से इब्राहिम लोदी को पराजित कर भारत में मुगल साम्राज्य की नींव रखी?
e:
The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526. Babur subsequently won Khanwa (1527 vs Rana Sanga), Chanderi (1528 vs Medini Rai), and Ghaghara (1529 vs Afghans).
• Exam Booster: Second Battle of Panipat = 1556 (Akbar/Bairam Khan vs Hemu); Third Battle of Panipat = 1761 (Ahmad Shah Abdali vs Marathas).
qe: In which year did the First Battle of Panipat take place, in which Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi using artillery and the Tulughma tactic to establish Mughal rule in India?

q: सम्राट अकबर के शासनकाल में 'दहसाला बंदोबस्त' (जब्ती / 10-वर्षीय भू-राजस्व व्यवस्था, 1580) किसने तैयार और लागू की?
e:
Akbar's finance minister Raja Todar Mal introduced the Ain-i-Dahsala (1580), fixing state revenue at 1/3rd of average produce over the preceding 10 years, classifying land into Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, and Banjar.
• Exam Booster: Akbar also introduced the Mansabdari system (Zat = personal rank/salary, Sawar = cavalry quota), Ibadat Khana (1575, Fatehpur Sikri), and Din-i-Ilahi (1582).
qe: Who designed and implemented the 'Dahsala System' (Zabti / 10-year land revenue settlement, 1580) during Emperor Akbar's reign?

q: किस शासक ने चाँदी का 'रुपया' (178 ग्रेन) चलाया, ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड (सड़क-ए-आजम) का निर्माण कराया, और जिनका अष्टकोणीय मकबरा सासाराम (बिहार) में स्थित है?
e:
Sher Shah Suri (1540–1545, defeated Humayun at Chausa 1539 and Bilgram/Kannauj 1540) introduced Patta & Qabuliyat, silver Rupiya, copper Dam, and postal Sarais.
• Exam Booster: Sher Shah died in 1545 from an accidental gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar fort (Banda, UP).
qe: Which ruler introduced the silver 'Rupiya' (178 grains), built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam from Sonargaon to Peshawar), and has his octagonal tomb at Sasaram (Bihar)?

q: किस मुगल सम्राट ने आगरा किले में 'न्याय की जंजीर' (जंजीर-ए-अदली) लगवाई थी और जिनके दरबार में अंग्रेज दूत कैप्टन विलियम हॉकिंस व सर थॉमस रो आए थे?
e:
Jahangir (1605–1627, autobiography 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' in Persian) established the golden Chain of Justice with 60 bells, granted Hawkins the title 'English Khan', and received Sir Thomas Roe (1615–18).
• Exam Booster: Jahangir's court painters Ustad Mansur (birds/flora) and Abul Hasan ('Nadir-uz-Zaman') marked the zenith of Mughal miniature painting.
qe: Which Mughal emperor issued the 'Chain of Justice' (जंजीर-ए-अदली) at Agra Fort and received English envoys Captain William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe?

q: औरंगजेब ने गैर-मुसलमानों पर 'जजिया' कर पुनः किस वर्ष लागू किया था (जिसे अकबर ने 1564 में समाप्त कर दिया था)?
e:
Aurangzeb re-imposed Jizya in 1679 CE. Earlier, Akbar had abolished Pilgrimage Tax in 1563 and Jizya in 1564.
• Exam Booster: Aurangzeb also annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687), and built Bibi ka Maqbara (Aurangabad) and Moti Masjid (Red Fort, Delhi).
qe: In which year did Aurangzeb re-impose the 'Jizya' tax on non-Muslims (which Akbar had abolished in 1564)?

q: भारत में ख्वाजा मोइनुद्दीन चिश्ती (अजमेर दरगाह) द्वारा किस सूफी सिलसिले की शुरुआत की गई, जिसमें बाबा फरीद और निजामुद्दीन औलिया शामिल थे?
e:
The Chishti Silsila emphasized love of God, service to humanity, Sama (devotional music), and staying aloof from royal courts.
• Exam Booster: Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi, 'Mehboob-e-Ilahi') famously told Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq "Hunuz Dilli Dur Ast" (Delhi is still far away).
qe: Which Sufi order (Silsila) was introduced in India by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (with its shrine at Ajmer) and included Baba Farid and Nizamuddin Auliya?

q: छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज के 'अष्टप्रधान' (आठ मंत्रियों की परिषद) में प्रधानमंत्री और विदेश मंत्री क्रमशः कौन कहलाते थे?
e:
In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan: Peshwa = Prime Minister; Sumant/Dabir = Foreign Minister; Amatya/Majumdar = Finance; Sar-i-Naubat = Commander-in-Chief.
• Exam Booster: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad in 1674; he levied 'Chauth' (1/4th) and 'Sardeshmukhi' (1/10th) on neighbouring territories.
qe: Under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's 'Ashtapradhan' (Council of Eight Ministers), who was the Prime Minister (head of civil & military affairs) and who was the Foreign Minister respectively?

q: जून 1665 में 'पुरंदर की संधि' किनके बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुई थी?
o: शिवाजी और मिर्जा राजा जयसिंह (औरंगजेब की ओर से)
e:
The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was signed between Shivaji and Mughal commander Mirza Raja Jai Singh, under which Shivaji ceded 23 of his 35 forts and agreed to visit Agra.
• Exam Booster: Another Treaty of Purandar (1776) was signed between the British East India Company and the Marathas during the First Anglo-Maratha War.
qe: Between whom was the 'Treaty of Purandar' signed in June 1665?
oe: Shivaji and Mirza Raja Jai Singh (representing Aurangzeb)

q: महाराष्ट्र के किस भक्ति संत ने 'अभंगों' की रचना की, जो शिवाजी के समकालीन थे और पंढरपुर के वारकरी संप्रदाय से संबंधित थे?
e:
Sant Tukaram (17th century) composed devotional Abhangas dedicated to Lord Vitthala (Vithoba) of Pandharpur.
• Exam Booster: Assam's Bhakti movement (Ekasarana Dharma) was led by Srimanta Shankaradeva; Bengal's Gaudiya Vaishnavism was led by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.
qe: Which Bhakti saint of Maharashtra composed the 'Abhangas', was a contemporary of Shivaji, and belonged to the Varkari sect of Pandharpur?

q: भारत में यूरोपीय व्यापारिक शक्तियों के आगमन का सही कालानुक्रम क्या है?
e:
Arrival order: Portuguese (Vasco da Gama, 1498 at Calicut) → Dutch (VOC 1602, first factory Masulipatnam 1605) → English (EIC 1600, Surat factory 1608/1613) → Danes (1616) → French (1664, Surat 1668).
• Exam Booster: Battle of Wandiwash (1760) decisively ended French political ambitions in India (Eyre Coote defeated Count de Lally).
qe: What is the correct chronological order of the arrival of European trading powers in India?

q:
भारत में निम्नलिखित ब्रिटिश भू-राजस्व व्यवस्थाओं को उनके प्रमुख प्रवर्तकों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. स्थायी बंदोबस्त (1793) — (a) हॉल्ट मैकेंजी / रॉबर्ट मर्टिन्स बर्ड
2. रैयतवाड़ी व्यवस्था (1820) — (b) लॉर्ड कार्नवालिस (सर जॉन शोर)
3. महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था (1822) — (c) थॉमस मुनरो और अलेक्जेंडर रीड
e:
Permanent Settlement (Bengal/Bihar/Orissa, ~19% area) — Cornwallis (1-b); Ryotwari (Madras/Bombay, ~51% area) — Thomas Munro & Alexander Read (2-c); Mahalwari (North-Western Provinces/UP & Punjab, ~30% area) — Holt Mackenzie & R. M. Bird (3-a).
• Exam Booster: Dadabhai Naoroji exposed British economic exploitation via the 'Drain of Wealth Theory' in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).
qe:
Match the following British land revenue systems in India with their principal architects:
1. Permanent Settlement (1793) — (a) Holt Mackenzie / Robert Merttins Bird
2. Ryotwari System (1820) — (b) Lord Cornwallis (Sir John Shore)
3. Mahalwari System (1822) — (c) Thomas Munro & Alexander Read

q: किस गवर्नर-जनरल ने 'सहायक संधि' (1798) लागू की और इसे स्वीकार करने वाली प्रथम भारतीय रियासत कौन-सी थी?
e:
Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798; Hyderabad was the first state to sign (1798), followed by Mysore (1799), Tanjore (1799), Awadh (1801), and Peshwa (Treaty of Bassein, 1802).
• Exam Booster: Note that French Governor Dupleix had earlier originated the practice of lending European troops to Indian princes, which Wellesley perfected.
qe: Which Governor-General introduced the 'Subsidiary Alliance' (सहायक संधि, 1798), and which was the first Indian princely state to accept it?

q: 10 मई 1857 को उत्तर प्रदेश के किस छावनी नगर से 1857 का विद्रोह एक संगठित सैनिक क्रांति के रूप में औपचारिक रूप से प्रारंभ हुआ?
e:
While Mangal Pandey's protest occurred at Barrackpore (Bengal) on 29 March 1857, the organized mass uprising began at Meerut (UP) on 10 May 1857 when sepoys marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar Emperor.
• Exam Booster: V. D. Savarkar called 1857 'The First War of Indian Independence'; R. C. Majumdar famously remarked it was "neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence".
qe: From which cantonment town of Uttar Pradesh did the Revolt of 1857 formally begin as an organized sepoy uprising on 10 May 1857?

q: 'वेदों की ओर लौटो' का प्रसिद्ध नारा किसने दिया और 'सत्यार्थ प्रकाश' की रचना किसने की?
e:
Swami Dayananda Saraswati (original name Mula Shankara) founded Arya Samaj in Bombay (1875), gave the call 'Back to the Vedas', and wrote 'Satyarth Prakash' in Hindi.
• Exam Booster: Swami Vivekananda addressed the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893 and founded Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
qe: Who gave the famous slogan 'Back to the Vedas' (वेदों की ओर लौटो) and authored 'Satyarth Prakash'?

q: ए. ओ. ह्यूम के प्रयासों से और व्योमेशचंद्र बनर्जी की अध्यक्षता में बंबई (गोकुलदास तेजपाल संस्कृत कॉलेज) में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस की स्थापना किस वर्ष हुई थी?
e:
The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 with 72 delegates during the Viceroyalty of Lord Dufferin.
• Exam Booster: First Muslim President = Badruddin Tyabji (1887, Madras); First European President = George Yule (1888, Allahabad); Only session presided by Mahatma Gandhi = Belgaum (1924).
qe: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded in Bombay (Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College) with A. O. Hume as founder and W. C. Bonnerjee as its first President?

q: दिसंबर 1929 में जवाहरलाल नेहरू की अध्यक्षता में कांग्रेस के किस अधिवेशन में 'पूर्ण स्वराज' का प्रस्ताव पारित किया गया था?
e:
The Lahore Session (Dec 1929, on the banks of the Ravi River) declared Purna Swaraj as the goal and fixed 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day.
• Exam Booster: Karachi Session (1931, Sardar Patel) passed the Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme resolution; Faizpur (1937) was the first session held in a village.
qe: At which session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru) was the 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution passed?

q: 1924 में कानपुर में शचींद्रनाथ सान्याल, रामप्रसाद बिस्मिल और जोगेशचंद्र चटर्जी द्वारा किस क्रांतिकारी संगठन की स्थापना की गई थी, जिसने काकोरी ट्रेन एक्शन (1925) को अंजाम दिया?
e:
HRA was founded in Kanpur (Oct 1924) and executed the Kakori Train Action (9 August 1925). Later in Sept 1928, Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh reorganized it as HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association) at Delhi.
• Exam Booster: Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco) — Lala Hardayal & Sohan Singh Bhakna; Abhinav Bharat (1904) — V. D. Savarkar.
qe: Which revolutionary organization was founded in Kanpur in 1924 by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil, and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, which carried out the Kakori Train Action (1925)?

q: किस ब्रिटिश प्रधानमंत्री ने 20 फरवरी 1947 को घोषणा की थी कि ब्रिटेन जून 1948 से पूर्व भारत को सत्ता हस्तांतरित कर देगा, और बाद में भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम 1947 पारित किया?
e:
Labour Prime Minister Clement Attlee made the 20 February 1947 declaration and appointed Lord Mountbatten, whose 3 June 1947 Plan led to the Indian Independence Act, 1947 (receiving Royal Assent on 18 July 1947).
• Exam Booster: C. Rajagopalachari became the first and last Indian Governor-General of independent India (1948–1950).
qe: Which British Prime Minister announced on 20 February 1947 that Britain would transfer power to India no later than June 1948, and subsequently passed the Indian Independence Act, 1947?

q: 1947 के बाद 560 से अधिक देशी रियासतों का भारतीय संघ में ऐतिहासिक एकीकरण किसने किया (वी. पी. मेनन के सहयोग से), जिन्हें 'भारत का लौह पुरुष' कहा जाता है?
e:
India's first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel integrated the princely states via the Instrument of Accession (including Junagadh via plebiscite, Hyderabad via Operation Polo in Sept 1948, and Jammu & Kashmir in Oct 1947).
• Exam Booster: National Unity Day (राष्ट्रीय एकता दिवस) is celebrated on 31 October (Sardar Patel's birth anniversary).
qe: Who led the historic integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union after 1947 (assisted by V. P. Menon), earning the title 'Iron Man of India'?

q: पोट्टी श्रीरामुलु के आमरण अनशन के बाद अक्टूबर 1953 में भाषाई आधार पर गठित होने वाला स्वतंत्र भारत का प्रथम राज्य कौन-सा बना, जिसके उपरांत राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम 1956 पारित हुआ?
e:
Andhra State (for Telugu speakers, carved out of Madras) was created on 1 October 1953. Subsequently, the Fazl Ali Commission (States Reorganisation Commission, 1953–55) led to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 creating 14 states and 6 UTs.
• Exam Booster: Earlier linguistic committees: Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, 1948–49).
qe: Which state became the first state in independent India to be formed on a linguistic basis in October 1953 (following the fast unto death of Potti Sriramulu), leading to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956?

q: 'पंचशील समझौता' (शांतिपूर्ण सह-अस्तित्व के पाँच सिद्धांत) 29 अप्रैल 1954 को भारत और किस देश के बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुआ था, जो बाद में 1955 के बांडुंग सम्मेलन का आधार बना?
e:
The Panchsheel Agreement was signed on 29 April 1954 between India (PM Jawaharlal Nehru) and China (Premier Zhou Enlai) regarding trade and intercourse between Tibet and India.
• Exam Booster: The 1955 Bandung Conference (Indonesia) laid the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM, first summit at Belgrade in 1961 — Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, Nkrumah).
qe: The 'Panchsheel Agreement' (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed on 29 April 1954 between India and which country, and later became a cornerstone of the 1955 Bandung Conference?

q: राजनीति विज्ञान में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा आधुनिक राज्य के चार अनिवार्य तत्वों में शामिल नहीं है?
e:
The four essential elements of a State (defined by Garner and Woodrow Wilson) are: Population, Definite Territory, Government, and Sovereignty. Sovereignty is the soul of the State; political parties are not an essential element.
• Exam Booster: Ancient Indian thinker Kautilya propounded the 'Saptanga Theory' of the State (7 elements: Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, Mitra).
qe: Which of the following is NOT one of the four essential elements of a modern State in Political Science?

q: अपनी पुस्तक 'लेक्चर्स ऑन ज्यूरिसप्रूडेंस' (1832) में 'एकलवादी संप्रभुता सिद्धांत' (कानून संप्रभु का आदेश है) किसने प्रतिपादित किया?
e:
English jurist John Austin propounded the Legal/Monistic Theory of Sovereignty (indivisible, absolute, inalienable). Jean Bodin coined the term 'Sovereignty' ('Six Books of the Republic', 1576).
• Exam Booster: Harold Laski, G. D. H. Cole, MacIver, and Maitland are Pluralist critics of Austin's monistic sovereignty ("Since society is federal, authority must also be federal" — Laski).
qe: Who propounded the 'Monistic Theory of Sovereignty' (एकलवादी संप्रभुता सिद्धांत) in his book 'Lectures on Jurisprudence' (1832), defining law as the command of the sovereign?

q: यह प्रसिद्ध कथन किसका है— "जहाँ कानून नहीं है, वहाँ स्वतंत्रता नहीं है"?
e:
John Locke ('Two Treatises of Government', 1689) wrote "Where there is no law, there is no freedom", emphasizing that rational law preserves and enlarges liberty rather than abolishing it.
• Exam Booster: Isaiah Berlin distinguished between 'Negative Liberty' (absence of external restraint) and 'Positive Liberty' (self-mastery) in 'Two Concepts of Liberty' (1958).
qe: Who famously remarked, "Where there is no law, there is no freedom" (जहाँ कानून नहीं, वहाँ स्वतंत्रता नहीं)?

q: "अधिकार सामाजिक जीवन की वे परिस्थितियाँ हैं जिनके बिना सामान्यतः कोई व्यक्ति अपना सर्वोत्तम विकास नहीं कर सकता।" — अधिकारों की यह प्रसिद्ध परिभाषा किसने दी?
e:
Harold J. Laski gave this classic definition of Rights in 'A Grammar of Politics' (1925), linking rights to social welfare and personality development.
• Exam Booster: John Locke propounded the Theory of Natural Rights (Life, Liberty, Property); Jeremy Bentham dismissed natural rights as "nonsense upon stilts" (Legal Theory of Rights).
qe: "Rights are those conditions of social life without which no man can seek, in general, to be himself at his best." — This celebrated definition of Rights was given by:

q: 'ए थ्योरी ऑफ जस्टिस' (1971) में जॉन रॉल्स ने मूल स्थिति में 'अज्ञान के पर्दे' (Veil of Ignorance) के विचार-प्रयोग की कल्पना मुख्यतः क्या व्युत्पन्न करने के लिए की?
o: दैवीय अधिकार पर आधारित निरंकुश राजतंत्र
निष्पक्षता के रूप में न्याय (अंतर सिद्धांत सहित, जो सबसे वंचित वर्ग के हित की रक्षा करता है)
e:
Behind the Veil of Ignorance, rational choosers do not know their class, wealth, gender, or talents, leading them to choose two principles of Justice as Fairness: (1) Equal Basic Liberties, and (2) Fair Equality of Opportunity + Difference Principle (inequalities justified only if they benefit the least advantaged).
• Exam Booster: Robert Nozick critiqued Rawls in 'Anarchy, State, and Utopia' (1974) with his Entitlement Theory of Justice.
qe: In 'A Theory of Justice' (1971), John Rawls introduced the thought experiment of the 'Veil of Ignorance' (अज्ञान का पर्दा) in the Original Position primarily to derive:
oe: Absolute monarchy based on divine right
Justice as Fairness (including the Difference Principle protecting the least advantaged)

q: 'इंट्रोडक्शन टू द स्टडी ऑफ द लॉ ऑफ द कॉन्स्टिट्यूशन' (1885) में 'विधि के शासन' (Rule of Law) की अवधारणा को किसने लोकप्रिय बनाया?
e:
British jurist A. V. Dicey articulated three pillars of Rule of Law: (1) Supremacy of Law (absence of arbitrary power), (2) Equality before Law, and (3) Predominance of Legal Spirit.
• Exam Booster: Montesquieu propounded the Theory of Separation of Powers ('The Spirit of Laws', 1748).
qe: Who popularized the concept of 'Rule of Law' (विधि का शासन) in 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' (1885)?

q: सीमित संवैधानिक सरकार, शासितों की सहमति और प्राकृतिक अधिकारों के समर्थन के कारण किस विचारक को 'उदारवाद का जनक' माना जाता है?
e:
John Locke is universally regarded as the Father of Classical Liberalism; Adam Smith ('Wealth of Nations', 1776) championed economic laissez-faire liberalism, while T. H. Green & Laski advanced Positive/Welfare Liberalism.
• Exam Booster: Classical liberalism views the state as a 'necessary evil' (night-watchman state), whereas Modern/Positive liberalism views it as a welfare institution.
qe: Which thinker is widely hailed as the 'Father of Liberalism' (उदारवाद के जनक) for championing limited constitutional government, consent of the governed, and natural rights?

q: कार्ल मार्क्स के 'ऐतिहासिक भौतिकवाद' के अनुसार समाज का 'आधार' (Base) और 'अधिरचना' (Superstructure) क्रमशः किससे निर्मित होते हैं?
o: आर्थिक उत्पादन प्रणाली (आधार) तथा राज्य, कानून, राजनीति, धर्म व विचारधारा (अधिरचना)
e:
Marx held that the economic mode of production (forces + relations of production) forms the material Base, which shapes the political, legal, cultural, and ideological Superstructure.
• Exam Booster: Marx borrowed 'Dialectics' from Hegel and 'Materialism' from Feuerbach to formulate Dialectical Materialism; his key works include 'Communist Manifesto' (1848, with Engels) and 'Das Kapital' (1867).
qe: According to Karl Marx's 'Historical Materialism' (ऐतिहासिक भौतिकवाद), what constitutes the 'Base' (आधार) and what constitutes the 'Superstructure' (अधिरचना) of society?
oe: Economic mode of production (Base) and State, law, politics, religion, ideology (Superstructure)

q: "सब कुछ राज्य के भीतर, राज्य के बाहर कुछ नहीं, राज्य के विरुद्ध कुछ नहीं" — यह सर्वाधिकारवादी कथन किस राजनीतिक विचारधारा और नेता से संबंधित है?
o: श्रेणी समाजवाद — जी. डी. एच. कोल
e:
Italian dictator Benito Mussolini formulated this defining slogan of Fascism (totalitarian, ultra-nationalist, anti-democratic, anti-Marxist).
• Exam Booster: German Idealist Hegel called the State "the march of God on earth"; Anarchists (Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin) advocate a stateless society.
qe: "Everything within the State, nothing outside the State, nothing against the State" — This totalitarian dictum is associated with which political ideology and leader?
oe: Guild Socialism — G. D. H. Cole

q: 1884 में ब्रिटेन में सिडनी व बीट्रिस वेब और जॉर्ज बर्नार्ड शॉ द्वारा स्थापित किस विकासवादी समाजवाद ने हिंसक क्रांति के बजाय क्रमिक संसदीय सुधार का समर्थन किया?
e:
Fabian Socialism (named after Roman general Fabius Cunctator for patient, gradual tactics) advocated democratic, constitutional transition to socialism and influenced the British Labour Party and Jawaharlal Nehru.
• Exam Booster: Robert Owen, Saint-Simon, and Charles Fourier were Utopian Socialists; Georges Sorel was associated with Syndicalism.
qe: Which brand of evolutionary democratic socialism—founded in Britain in 1884 by Sidney & Beatrice Webb and George Bernard Shaw—advocated gradual parliamentary reform rather than violent revolution?

q: महात्मा गांधी का वह आर्थिक सिद्धांत जिसके अनुसार धनी उद्योगपतियों और जमींदारों को अपनी अतिरिक्त संपत्ति को समाज के कल्याण हेतु धरोहर के रूप में रखना चाहिए, क्या कहलाता है?
e:
Gandhi's Doctrine of Trusteeship (न्यासिता सिद्धांत) seeks voluntary economic justice without violent expropriation, grounded in Aparigraha (non-possession) and Sarvodaya (welfare of all).
• Exam Booster: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was inspired by John Ruskin's book 'Unto This Last'; his 'Civil Disobedience' drew inspiration from Henry David Thoreau.
qe: Mahatma Gandhi's economic doctrine that wealthy industrialists and landlords should hold their surplus wealth as custodians for the welfare of society is known as:

q: किसे सर्वमान्य रूप से 'राजनीति विज्ञान का जनक' माना जाता है, जिन्होंने सरकारों का वर्गीकरण राजतंत्र, कुलीनतंत्र, पॉलिटी (और उनके विकृत रूप निरंकुशतंत्र, अल्पतंत्र, भीड़तंत्र) में किया?
e:
Aristotle ('The Politics', disciple of Plato, teacher of Alexander) called Political Science the 'Master Science' and defined man as a "political animal" (Zoon Politikon).
• Exam Booster: Plato ('The Republic', 'The Statesman', 'The Laws') proposed the Philosopher King, Theory of Justice, and Communism of Property & Wives for the Guardian class.
qe: Who is universally recognized as the 'Father of Political Science' and classified governments into Monarchy, Aristocracy, Polity (and their perverted forms Tyranny, Oligarchy, Democracy)?

q:
निम्नलिखित सामाजिक समझौता विचारकों को उनके प्रमुख ग्रंथों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. थॉमस हॉब्स — (a) द सोशल कॉन्ट्रैक्ट (1762)
2. जॉन लॉक — (b) लेवियाथन (1651)
3. ज्याँ-जैक रूसो — (c) टू ट्रीटाइजेज ऑफ गवर्नमेंट (1689)
e:
Hobbes — Leviathan (1-b, absolute sovereignty); Locke — Two Treatises of Government (2-c, limited constitutional sovereignty); Rousseau — The Social Contract (3-a, Popular Sovereignty & General Will / सामान्य इच्छा).
• Exam Booster: Rousseau's famous opening line: "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains."
qe:
Match the following Social Contract thinkers with their landmark treatises:
1. Thomas Hobbes — (a) The Social Contract (1762)
2. John Locke — (b) Leviathan (1651)
3. Jean-Jacques Rousseau — (c) Two Treatises of Government (1689)

q: 'ऑन लिबर्टी' (1859) में जॉन स्टुअर्ट मिल ने 'स्व-संबंधी कार्यों' और 'पर-संबंधी कार्यों' में अंतर किया, तथा 'कंसीडरेशंस ऑन रिप्रेजेंटेटिव गवर्नमेंट' (1861) में उन्होंने किसका समर्थन किया?
o: बिना शैक्षणिक योग्यता के गुप्त मतदान
संसद का उन्मूलन और निरंकुश राजतंत्र
आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व (हेयर प्रणाली), बहुल मतदान और महिला मताधिकार
e:
J. S. Mill was a staunch champion of individual liberty, women's suffrage ('The Subjection of Women', 1869), Proportional Representation (to protect minorities from tyranny of the majority), Open Ballot, and Plural Voting (extra votes for educated citizens).
• Exam Booster: Unlike Bentham's purely quantitative utilitarianism ("push-pin is as good as poetry"), Mill introduced QUALITATIVE differences in pleasures ("Better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a pig satisfied").
qe: In 'On Liberty' (1859), John Stuart Mill distinguished between 'Self-regarding actions' and 'Other-regarding actions', and in 'Considerations on Representative Government' (1861) he supported:
oe: Abolition of Parliament and absolute monarchy
Proportional Representation (Hare System), Plural Voting, and Women's Suffrage

q: अपनी कृति 'द प्रिंस' (1513) में राजनीति को धर्म और नैतिकता से पृथक करने के कारण किसे 'प्रथम आधुनिक राजनीतिक विचारक' माना जाता है?
e:
Italian Renaissance thinker Niccolò Machiavelli ('The Prince', 'Discourses on Livy') separated political statecraft from theology/ethics and advised the ruler to combine the qualities of a Lion (force) and a Fox (cunning).
• Exam Booster: Kautilya is often compared to Machiavelli ('Indian Machiavelli'), though Kautilya's Arthashastra predates Machiavelli by ~1,800 years.
qe: Who is regarded as the 'First Modern Political Thinker' for separating politics from religion and morality in his treatise 'The Prince' (1513)?

q: कौटिल्य के अर्थशास्त्र में वर्णित 'मंडल सिद्धांत' मुख्य रूप से किससे संबंधित है?
o: विदेश नीति, अंतर्राज्यीय संबंध और भू-राजनीति (विजिगीषु, अरि, मित्र)
e:
Kautilya's Mandala Theory outlines a circle of 12 states centered on the aspiring conqueror ('Vijigishu'), operating on the realist maxim that an immediate neighbour is a natural enemy ('Ari') and the neighbour's neighbour is a natural ally ('Mitra').
• Exam Booster: Kautilya also outlined the 'Shadgunya' (6-fold foreign policy: Sandhi, Vigraha, Asana, Yana, Samshraya, Dvaidhibhava) and 4 Upayas (Sama, Dama, Danda, Bheda).
qe: Kautilya's 'Mandala Theory' (मंडल सिद्धांत) in the Arthashastra deals primarily with:
oe: Foreign policy, interstate relations, and geopolitics (Vijigishu, Ari, Mitra)

q: 'मनुस्मृति' में मनु की 'दंड' और 'राजधर्म' की अवधारणा किस बात पर बल देती है?
o: राजा भी धर्म के अधीन है, और दंड वह संप्रभु नैतिक शक्ति है जो धर्म व सामाजिक व्यवस्था की रक्षा करती है
राजा सभी नैतिक नियमों से ऊपर है और केवल व्यक्तिगत इच्छा से कार्य करता है
शांतिकाल में कर कृषि उपज का 50% से अधिक होना चाहिए
कार्यपालिका और न्यायिक कर्तव्यों में कोई अंतर नहीं होना चाहिए
e:
Manu regards Dharma as supreme over the ruler himself; 'Danda' (just punishment/coercive authority) enforces Rajadharma and prevents 'Matsyanyaya' (law of the fishes, where the strong devour the weak).
• Exam Booster: Like Kautilya, Manu also accepts the Saptanga theory of the State and Mandala theory of foreign relations.
qe: In 'Manusmriti', Manu's concept of 'Danda' (दंड) and 'Rajadharma' emphasizes that:
oe: Even the King is subordinate to Dharma, and Danda is the sovereign moral instrument that protects Dharma and social order
The King is above all moral law and acts purely on personal whim
Taxation should exceed 50% of agricultural produce in peacetime
There should be no distinction between executive and judicial duties

q: जेरेमी बेंथम का 'उपयोगितावाद' किस आधारभूत सिद्धांत द्वारा संक्षेपित किया जाता है?
o: प्रत्येक से उसकी क्षमता के अनुसार, प्रत्येक को उसकी आवश्यकता के अनुसार
e:
Jeremy Bentham ('An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation', 1789) proposed the Felicific Calculus to measure pleasure quantitatively and maximize "the greatest happiness of the greatest number".
• Exam Booster: Option B is Karl Marx's communist principle ('Critique of the Gotha Programme'); Option C is Herbert Spencer's Social Darwinism.
qe: Jeremy Bentham's 'Utilitarianism' (उपयोगितावाद) is summarized by which foundational principle?
oe: The greatest happiness of the greatest number
From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs

q: अध्यक्षात्मक शासन प्रणाली (जैसे अमेरिका) की तुलना में 'संसदीय शासन प्रणाली' (जैसे भारत और ब्रिटेन) की मूल विशिष्टता क्या है?
o: कार्यपालिका (मंत्रिपरिषद) का विधायिका के प्रति सामूहिक उत्तरदायित्व
कार्यपालिका और विधायिका के बीच कठोर शक्ति-पृथक्करण
कार्यपालिका प्रमुख का निश्चित अपरिवर्तनीय कार्यकाल
e:
In a Parliamentary system, the Executive is drawn from and is collectively responsible to the Legislature (Article 75(3) in India), and there is a dual executive (nominal Head of State + real Head of Government).
• Exam Booster: Presidential system features strict separation of powers, single executive (President is both Head of State and Government), and fixed tenure.
qe: What is the core distinguishing feature of a 'Parliamentary Form of Government' (as in India and the UK) compared to a Presidential system (as in the USA)?
oe: Collective responsibility of the Executive (Council of Ministers) to the Legislature
Strict separation of powers between Executive and Legislature
Fixed, irremovable tenure of the executive head
Absence of a nominal Head of State

q: भारत के संविधान को किसने 'अर्ध-संघात्मक' (Quasi-Federal) — "सहायक संघीय विशेषताओं वाला एकात्मक राज्य" — कहा था?
e:
Constitutional scholar K. C. Wheare termed India 'Quasi-Federal'.
• Exam Booster: Granville Austin called Indian federalism 'Cooperative Federalism'; Morris Jones called it 'Bargaining Federalism'; Ivor Jennings called it 'Federation with a strong centralizing tendency'.
qe: Who famously described the Constitution of India as 'Quasi-Federal' (अर्ध-संघात्मक) — "a unitary state with subsidiary federal features rather than a federal state with subsidiary unitary features"?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी एक सच्चे संघात्मक संविधान की अनिवार्य विशेषता नहीं है?
o: केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच शक्तियों का विभाजन
केंद्र-राज्य विवादों के निपटारे हेतु स्वतंत्र न्यायपालिका
एकल नागरिकता और अखिल भारतीय सेवाएँ
e:
Single Citizenship and All-India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS) are UNITARY (एकात्मक) features of the Indian Constitution, whereas a classic federation (like the USA) has Dual Citizenship and separate federal/state services.
• Exam Booster: Other unitary features of India: Integrated Judiciary, Appointment of Governors by Centre, Emergency provisions (Arts 352, 356, 360).
qe: Which of the following is NOT an essential characteristic of a true Federal Constitution?
oe: Division of powers between Centre and States
Independent Judiciary to settle Centre–State disputes

q: प्रत्यक्ष लोकतंत्र (जैसे स्विट्जरलैंड) में वह उपकरण क्या कहलाता है जिसके द्वारा नागरिक स्वयं किसी प्रस्तावित कानून का मसौदा तैयार कर विधायिका या मतदाताओं को उस पर मतदान के लिए बाध्य कर सकते हैं?
e:
Initiative (आरंभक) empowers citizens to initiate legislation; Referendum submits a legislative bill to popular vote; Recall allows voters to remove an elected representative before term completion.
• Exam Booster: Abraham Lincoln defined democracy as "government of the people, by the people, for the people" (Gettysburg Address, 1863).
qe: In direct democracies (such as Switzerland), what is the device by which citizens themselves can draft a proposed law and compel the legislature or electorate to vote on it?

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत संसद, राज्य विधानमंडल, राष्ट्रपति और उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनावों के संचालन हेतु स्वतंत्र 'भारत निर्वाचन आयोग' (ECI) की स्थापना की गई है?
e:
Article 324 establishes the Election Commission of India (founded 25 January 1950 — celebrated as National Voters' Day; multi-member body since 1993: 1 CEC + 2 ECs).
• Exam Booster: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the STATE Election Commission (Articles 243K & 243ZA), NOT by the ECI!
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the independent 'Election Commission of India' (ECI) established to superintend and conduct Parliament, State Legislature, President, and Vice-President elections?

q: भारत में लोकसभा एवं राज्य विधानसभा चुनावों के लिए कौन-सी निर्वाचन प्रणाली प्रयुक्त होती है, और राष्ट्रपति व राज्यसभा के लिए कौन-सी प्रणाली प्रयुक्त होती है?
o: लोकसभा/विधानसभा हेतु अग्रता ही विजेता (FPTP); राष्ट्रपति/राज्यसभा हेतु एकल संक्रमणीय मत द्वारा आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व
लोकसभा हेतु सूची प्रणाली और राष्ट्रपति हेतु FPTP
e:
Direct elections to Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabhas use the simple plurality First-Past-the-Post (FPTP) system, while indirect elections to President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha, and Vidhan Parishads use Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV).
• Exam Booster: Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990), Tarkunde Committee (1974), and Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) are landmark committees on Electoral Reforms in India.
qe: Which electoral system is used in India for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, and which system is used for the President and Rajya Sabha?
oe: First-Past-the-Post (FPTP) for Lok Sabha/Assemblies; Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) for President/Rajya Sabha
List System for Lok Sabha and FPTP for President

q: 'राजनीतिक दल' और 'दबाव समूह' (हित समूह) के बीच प्राथमिक कार्यात्मक अंतर क्या है?
o: राजनीतिक दल सत्ता प्राप्त करने हेतु चुनाव लड़ते हैं, जबकि दबाव समूह चुनाव लड़े बिना बाहर से सार्वजनिक नीति को प्रभावित करते हैं
सभी लोकतांत्रिक संविधानों में दबाव समूह प्रतिबंधित हैं
राजनीतिक दल केवल एक ही व्यावसायिक वर्ग का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं
दबाव समूह संसद में मंत्रिपरिषद का गठन करते हैं
e:
Political parties aim to capture and exercise formal government power via elections; Pressure groups (e.g., FICCI, AITUC, BKU, Bar Council) lobby and mobilize opinion to protect specific group interests without seeking office.
• Exam Booster: Gabriel Almond classified pressure groups into Institutional, Associational, Non-associational, and Anomic groups.
qe: What is the primary functional difference between a 'Political Party' and a 'Pressure Group' (Interest Group)?
oe: Political parties contest elections to capture political power, whereas pressure groups influence public policy from outside without contesting elections
Pressure groups are banned in all democratic constitutions
Political parties represent only a single occupational group
Pressure groups form the Council of Ministers in Parliament

q: "स्वराज मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूँगा" — यह ओजस्वी राष्ट्रवादी उद्घोष किसने दिया था?
e:
Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave this famous slogan (popularized during the Home Rule Movement, 1916); he started newspapers 'Kesari' (Marathi) and 'Mahratta' (English) and wrote 'Gita Rahasya' in Mandalay Jail.
• Exam Booster: Gopal Krishna Gokhale (founder of Servants of India Society, 1905) was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.
qe: Who gave the inspiring nationalist slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it" (स्वराज मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूँगा)?

q: भारतीय संविधान की प्रारूप समिति के अध्यक्ष कौन थे, जिन्होंने 'एनिहिलेशन ऑफ कास्ट' लिखी और इंडिपेंडेंट लेबर पार्टी (1936) व शेड्यूल्ड कास्ट्स फेडरेशन (1942) की स्थापना की?
e:
Bharat Ratna Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee (appointed 29 August 1947) and is revered as the Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution.
• Exam Booster: Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly; Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee & Union Constitution Committee.
qe: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution, authored 'Annihilation of Caste', and founded the Independent Labour Party (1936) and Scheduled Castes Federation (1942)?

q: 13 दिसंबर 1946 को संविधान सभा में ऐतिहासिक 'उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव' किसने प्रस्तुत किया था, जो बाद में भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना का आधार बना?
e:
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946, which was unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 January 1947.
• Exam Booster: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into full force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
qe: Who moved the historic 'Objectives Resolution' (उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव) in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946, which later evolved into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?

q: भारत ने 'मौलिक अधिकार', 'न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन' और 'राष्ट्रपति पर महाभियोग' की अवधारणाएँ किस देश के संविधान से ग्रहण की हैं?
e:
USA = Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review, Independence of Judiciary, Impeachment of President, Vice-President post.
• Exam Booster: UK = Parliamentary system, Rule of Law, Single Citizenship; Canada = Federation with strong Centre & Residuary powers with Centre; Australia = Concurrent List & Joint Sitting; USSR = Fundamental Duties.
qe: From which country's Constitution did India borrow the concepts of 'Fundamental Rights', 'Judicial Review', and 'Impeachment of the President'?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा 'संपत्ति के अधिकार' को मौलिक अधिकारों की सूची से हटाकर अनुच्छेद 300A के अंतर्गत एक विधिक अधिकार बना दिया गया?
e:
The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 (Janata Party government) shifted Right to Property from Part III to Article 300A (Part XII), leaving 6 Fundamental Rights.
• Exam Booster: The 44th Amendment also replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352 and ensured Articles 20 & 21 cannot be suspended even during National Emergency.
qe: By which Constitutional Amendment was the 'Right to Property' removed from the list of Fundamental Rights (Articles 19(1)(f) and 31) and made a legal right under Article 300A?

q: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के किस ऐतिहासिक 13-न्यायाधीशों वाले निर्णय (1973) में 'मूल ढाँचे का सिद्धांत' प्रतिपादित किया गया, जिसमें कहा गया कि संसद अनुच्छेद 368 के तहत संविधान के मूल ढाँचे को नष्ट नहीं कर सकती?
o: ए. के. गोपालन बनाम मद्रास राज्य
e:
In Kesavananda Bharati (24 April 1973, 7–6 majority), the Supreme Court overruled Golaknath and established the Basic Structure Doctrine (supremacy of Constitution, secularism, federalism, judicial review, democracy).
• Exam Booster: Minerva Mills (1980) reaffirmed the balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSP as part of the Basic Structure.
qe: In which landmark 13-judge Supreme Court judgment (1973) was the 'Basic Structure Doctrine' (मूल ढाँचे का सिद्धांत) propounded, ruling that Parliament cannot alter the basic framework of the Constitution under Article 368?
oe: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills vs Union of India (1980)
A. K. Gopalan vs State of Madras (1950)

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद राज्य को लोक सेवाओं में न्यायपालिका को कार्यपालिका से पृथक करने के लिए कदम उठाने का निर्देश देता है?
e:
Article 50 (DPSP) mandates separation of judiciary from executive.
• Exam Booster: Article 40 = Village Panchayats; Article 44 = Uniform Civil Code; Article 48A = Environment & Wildlife protection; Article 51 = Promotion of international peace and security.
qe: Which Article of the Indian Constitution directs the State to take steps to separate the Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State?

q: अनुच्छेद 54 के अंतर्गत भारत के राष्ट्रपति के निर्वाचन हेतु निर्वाचक मंडल (Electoral College) में कौन शामिल होता है?
o: संसद के दोनों सदनों के निर्वाचित सदस्य तथा राज्यों (दिल्ली व पुडुचेरी सहित) की विधानसभाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्य
केवल संसद के सभी निर्वाचित और मनोनीत सदस्य
लोकसभा और राज्य विधान परिषदों के सदस्य
प्रत्यक्ष रूप से भारत के सभी वयस्क नागरिक
e:
Nominated members of Parliament/Assemblies and members of State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad) do NOT vote in the Presidential election.
• Exam Booster: By contrast, in the Vice-President's election (Article 66), ALL members (both elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament vote, and State Assemblies do NOT participate.
qe: Who participates in the Electoral College for electing the President of India under Article 54?
oe: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi & Puducherry)
All elected and nominated members of Parliament only
Members of Lok Sabha and State Legislative Councils
Directly all adult citizens of India

q: अनुच्छेद 85 के अंतर्गत भारतीय संसद के दो क्रमागत सत्रों के बीच अधिकतम अनुमत समय अंतराल कितना है?
e:
Article 85 mandates that not more than 6 months shall intervene between the last sitting in one session and the first sitting in the next session (hence Parliament must meet at least twice a year; traditionally 3 sessions: Budget, Monsoon, Winter).
• Exam Booster: Quorum for either House of Parliament is 1/10th (10%) of total membership (Article 100).
qe: What is the maximum permissible time gap between two consecutive sessions of the Indian Parliament under Article 85?

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत भारत के राष्ट्रपति सार्वजनिक महत्व के किसी विधि या तथ्य के प्रश्न पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय से परामर्श (सलाहकारी क्षेत्राधिकार) माँग सकते हैं?
e:
Article 143 vests Advisory Jurisdiction in the Supreme Court (borrowed from Canada); the Court's advisory opinion is not legally binding on the President.
• Exam Booster: Article 124 = Establishment of SC; Article 131 = Original Jurisdiction (Centre–State / Inter-State disputes); Article 137 = Review of judgments by SC; Article 142 = Complete Justice.
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance?

q: भारतीय संविधान के आपात उपबंधों (भाग XVIII) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: अनुच्छेद 352 के तहत राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल तीन बार (1962, 1971, 1975) घोषित हुआ है
राज्य में राष्ट्रपति शासन अनुच्छेद 356 के अंतर्गत लगाया जाता है
अनुच्छेद 360 के तहत वित्तीय आपातकाल भारत में दो बार घोषित किया जा चुका है
राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल की उद्घोषणा को 1 माह के भीतर संसद के दोनों सदनों द्वारा विशेष बहुमत से अनुमोदित होना आवश्यक है
e:
Statement C is NOT correct: Financial Emergency under Article 360 has NEVER been proclaimed in India since 1950! Statements A, B, and D are all accurate. (भारत में अनुच्छेद 360 के अंतर्गत वित्तीय आपातकाल आज तक कभी नहीं लगा है।)
• Exam Booster: President's Rule (Art 356) requires parliamentary approval within 2 months by simple majority.
qe: Which of the following statements regarding Emergency Provisions (Part XVIII) of the Indian Constitution is NOT correct?
oe: National Emergency under Article 352 has been proclaimed three times (1962, 1971, 1975)
President's Rule in a State is imposed under Article 356
Financial Emergency under Article 360 has been declared twice in India
A proclamation of National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 1 month by special majority

q:
भारत के निम्नलिखित संवैधानिक निकायों को उनके संबंधित अनुच्छेदों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) — (a) अनुच्छेद 280
2. भारत के महान्यायवादी (Attorney General) — (b) अनुच्छेद 315
3. वित्त आयोग — (c) अनुच्छेद 148
4. संघ लोक सेवा आयोग (UPSC) — (d) अनुच्छेद 76
e:
Correct matching: CAG — Article 148 (1-c); Attorney General — Article 76 (2-d); Finance Commission — Article 280 (3-a); UPSC — Article 315 (4-b).
• Exam Booster: Advocate General of a State is appointed under Article 165.
qe:
Match the following Constitutional Bodies of India with their respective Articles:
1. Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) — (a) Article 280
2. Attorney General of India — (b) Article 315
3. Finance Commission — (c) Article 148
4. Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) — (d) Article 76

q: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम (1992) ने पंचायती राज संस्थाओं (भाग IX, 11वीं अनुसूची — 29 विषय) को संवैधानिक दर्जा प्रदान किया?
e:
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (effective 24 April 1993 — National Panchayati Raj Day) established the 3-tier Panchayati Raj system (Gram, Block/Kshetra, Zila) with 1/3rd mandatory women's reservation.
• Exam Booster: 74th Amendment (1992) = Urban Local Bodies/Municipalities (Part IXA, 12th Schedule — 18 subjects). Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended 3-tier PRIs; Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959) was the first state to adopt PRIs.
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (Part IX, 11th Schedule — 29 subjects)?

q: अनुच्छेद 164(1A) (91वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 2003 द्वारा अंतःस्थापित) के अंतर्गत किसी राज्य की मंत्रिपरिषद में मुख्यमंत्री सहित मंत्रियों की कुल संख्या विधानसभा की कुल सदस्य संख्या के कितने प्रतिशत से अधिक नहीं हो सकती?
e:
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the strength of the Lok Sabha (Union, Art 75(1A)) and State Legislative Assembly (States, Art 164(1A), with a minimum of 12 ministers for small states).
• Exam Booster: In Delhi (NCT), the cap is 10% (7 ministers out of 70 MLAs) under Article 239AA.
qe: Under Article 164(1A) (inserted by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003), the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed what percentage of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly?

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत यदि किसी राज्य की विधानसभा विशेष बहुमत से संकल्प पारित करे, तो संसद उस राज्य में विधान परिषद (Legislative Council) का सृजन या उत्सादन कर सकती है?
e:
Article 169 empowers Parliament (by simple majority — NOT a constitutional amendment under Art 368) to create or abolish a Vidhan Parishad following a special-majority resolution of the Vidhan Sabha.
• Exam Booster: Article 171 specifies the composition of Vidhan Parishad (max 1/3rd of Assembly strength, min 40; 1/6th nominated by Governor).
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can Parliament create or abolish a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) if the State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority?

q: किस समिति (1986) ने सर्वप्रथम औपचारिक रूप से पंचायती राज संस्थाओं को 'संवैधानिक दर्जा' प्रदान करने की अनुशंसा की थी (जिससे अंततः 73वाँ संशोधन हुआ)?
e:
The L. M. Singhvi Committee (1986, appointed by Rajiv Gandhi government) recommended constitutional recognition for PRIs and Gram Sabhas as the embodiment of direct democracy.
• Exam Booster: Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) had recommended a 2-tier system (Zila Parishad & Mandal Panchayat) and official participation of political parties.
qe: Which committee (1986) was the first to formally recommend granting 'Constitutional Status' to Panchayati Raj Institutions (which eventually led to the 73rd Amendment)?

q: भारत में लोक सेवकों के विरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार के आरोपों की जाँच हेतु लोकपाल एवं लोकायुक्त अधिनियम 2013 पारित किया गया। वर्ष 2019 में भारत के प्रथम लोकपाल कौन नियुक्त हुए थे?
e:
Former Supreme Court judge Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was appointed India's first Lokpal in March 2019. (Maharashtra was the first state to establish a Lokayukta in 1971; Odisha passed the first Act in 1970.)
• Exam Booster: The Ombudsman institution originated in Sweden in 1809; the term 'Lokpal' in India was coined by L. M. Singhvi (1963) and recommended by the First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966).
qe: The institution of 'Lokpal' (Ombudsman) in India was enacted under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 to investigate allegations of corruption against public functionaries. Who was appointed as India's FIRST Lokpal in 2019?

q: स्वतंत्रता के बाद से निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा भारत की विदेश नीति का आधारभूत सिद्धांत नहीं है?
o: उपनिवेशवाद और नस्लीय भेदभाव का विरोध
नाटो जैसे स्थायी सैन्य गुटों में शामिल होना
e:
India's foreign policy has consistently rejected joining Cold War or permanent military bloc alliances, preferring Non-Alignment, Panchsheel, Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, and Strategic Autonomy.
• Exam Booster: Article 51 (DPSP) constitutionally enshrines India's commitment to international peace, just relations, and arbitration of international disputes.
qe: Which of the following is NOT a foundational principle of India's Foreign Policy since independence?
oe: Opposition to colonialism and racial discrimination
Joining permanent military bloc alliances like NATO

q: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद (UNSC) में वीटो शक्ति प्राप्त कितने स्थायी सदस्य (P5) हैं, और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय (ICJ) का मुख्यालय कहाँ स्थित है?
e:
UNSC has 15 members: 5 Permanent veto-holders (USA, UK, France, Russia, China) + 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms. The ICJ (15 judges, 9-year term) is headquartered at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands—the only principal UN organ outside New York.
• Exam Booster: UN was founded on 24 October 1945 (UN Day); India is a founding member.
qe: How many permanent veto-holding members (P5) sit on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), and where is the International Court of Justice (ICJ) headquartered?

q: दसवीं अनुसूची (दलबदल विरोधी कानून, 52वाँ संशोधन 1985, 91वें संशोधन 2003 द्वारा संशोधित) के अंतर्गत किसी राजनीतिक दल के विधायी सदस्यों के न्यूनतम कितने अंश द्वारा किसी अन्य दल में 'विलय' (Merger) पर सहमति होने पर वे अयोग्यता से मुक्त रहते हैं?
e:
The 91st Amendment (2003) deleted the earlier 1/3rd 'split' exemption and retained only the 'merger' exemption requiring at least TWO-THIRDS (2/3) of the legislature party members to agree to merge.
• Exam Booster: Disqualification questions under the 10th Schedule are decided by the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman), whose decision is subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan case, 1992).
qe: Under the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law, 52nd Amendment 1985, modified by 91st Amendment 2003), what minimum fraction of a political party's legislative members must agree to a 'Merger' with another party to be exempt from disqualification?
